description: Binomial and lattice models: one-period replication, the CRR tree and its convergence, American options on the tree. `chapter` is the section number the entry had in the original single-file corpus, not a chapter of one book; each entry's `reference` names its source.
alignment_source: Several works: each entry's `reference` names its source (textbooks, papers and regulatory texts in mathematical finance)

theorems.name: Single-Period Binomial Replication Theorem
theorems.description: In a single-period binomial model with no-arbitrage (d < e^r < u), every contingent claim with payoffs (V_u, V_d) in the up/down states is replicable, and the replicating portfolio cost equals the risk-neutral expected payoff discounted: V_0 = e^{-r} (q V_u + (1-q) V_d) where q = (e^r - d) / (u - d).

metadata.reference: Single-period binomial replication (Cox-Ross-Rubinstein 1979; Shreve I 1.2)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of all three statements: portfolio cost, up-state payoff, down-state payoff. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/Model.lean. Axioms-clean. Multi-period backward induction (binomialPrice) also defined and proved consistent; CRR convergence to BS is upstream.

theorems.name: CRR One-Step Risk-Neutral Martingale Identity
theorems.description: Under CRR parameterization (u_n = e^{σ √Δt}, d_n = e^{-σ √Δt}, Δt = T/n), the risk-neutral up-probability p_n = (e^{rΔt} - d_n)/(u_n - d_n) satisfies p_n · u_n + (1 - p_n) · d_n = e^{rΔt}. The discrete-time discounted asset is a Q-martingale at each step. Exact algebraic identity, not asymptotic.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.CRRConvergence

open MathFin

/-- CRR one-step risk-neutral martingale identity. -/
theorem crr_one_step_martingale_identity {σ T r : ℝ} {n : ℕ}
    (h_du : crrDown σ T n < crrUp σ T n) :
    crrProb r σ T n * crrUp σ T n + (1 - crrProb r σ T n) * crrDown σ T n
      = Real.exp (crrPerStepRate r T n) :=
  MathFin.crr_one_step_martingale h_du

metadata.reference: CRR parameterization, one-step martingale (Hull 21.1, Shreve I 1.2)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Pure algebraic identity following from the definitions of crrUp, crrDown, crrPerStepRate, crrProb. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/CRRConvergence.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: CRR Risk-Neutral Probability Tends to 1/2
theorems.description: Under the CRR parameterization with σ > 0 and T > 0, the risk-neutral up-probability p_n → 1/2 as n → ∞: the per-step Bernoulli increment becomes asymptotically symmetric. This is the analytic step behind the variance limit n · σ² Δt · 4 p_n (1 - p_n) → σ² T in the CRR-to-Black–Scholes correspondence; that limit is not itself stated in this entry.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.CRRConvergence

open MathFin Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- CRR risk-neutral probability tends to 1/2 as n → ∞. -/
theorem crr_prob_tendsto_half {σ T r : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => crrProb r σ T n) Filter.atTop (𝓝 (1/2)) :=
  MathFin.crrProb_tendsto_half hσ hT

metadata.reference: CRR convergence (analytic step), Hull 21.1, Shreve I 3.2
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Substantial: ~80 lines using difference-quotient limits (e^{cx}-1)/x → c via hasDerivAt_iff_tendsto_slope, plus quotient-of-limits arithmetic to show p(h) → 1/2 as h → 0, plus composition with h_n = √(T/n). Implies the variance limit. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/CRRConvergence.lean. Axioms-clean. The full distributional convergence binomialPrice → bs_call_price is now proved: see mf-crr-gaussian-limit and mf-crr-bs-call-convergence.

theorems.name: CRR Variance Limit
theorems.description: Under CRR parameterization, n · σ² · (T/n) · 4 p_n (1 - p_n) → σ² T as n → ∞. The per-step variance of the log-return matches the BS variance to leading order. Direct corollary of crrProb_tendsto_half.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.CRRConvergence

open MathFin Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- CRR variance limit: 4 σ² T · p_n (1 - p_n) → σ² T. -/
theorem crr_variance_limit_theorem {σ T r : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    Filter.Tendsto
      (fun n : ℕ => 4 * σ^2 * T * (crrProb r σ T n) * (1 - crrProb r σ T n))
      Filter.atTop (𝓝 (σ^2 * T)) :=
  MathFin.crr_variance_limit hσ hT

metadata.reference: CRR variance convergence (Hull 21.1, Shreve I 3.2)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Direct corollary of crrProb_tendsto_half via 4 p_n (1 - p_n) → 4 · (1/2) · (1/2) = 1, then const_mul to get σ² T. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/CRRConvergence.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: CRR to Black-Scholes: Log-Return Convergence in Distribution
theorems.description: Whenever every step's risk-neutral up-probability is a genuine probability (0 ≤ pₙ ≤ 1 — the non-strict closure of the no-arbitrage condition, which the degenerate n = 0 step satisfies), the law of the n-step CRR risk-neutral log-return — the n-fold convolution of the two-point per-step law — converges weakly to the Black-Scholes normal N((r − σ²/2)T, σ²T). The genuine distributional CLT for the binomial tree, via characteristic functions and Lévy's continuity theorem.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.CRRCharFun

open MathFin Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- CRR → Black–Scholes, convergence in distribution: under no-arbitrage at every
    step (`0 ≤ pₙ ≤ 1`), the `n`-step CRR risk-neutral log-return law — the `n`-fold
    convolution `crrRowProbMeasure` of the two-point per-step law — converges weakly
    to the Black–Scholes normal `N((r − σ²/2)T, σ²T)`. Re-export of
    `MathFin.crr_tendsto_gaussian_inDistribution` (real derivation in
    `MathFin/Binomial/CRRCharFun.lean`: the per-step charFun is computed exactly,
    its `n`-th power converges to the Gaussian charFun
    (`crr_charFun_pow_tendsto_gaussian`), and Lévy's continuity theorem
    (`ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_of_tendsto_charFun`) upgrades charFun convergence
    to weak convergence, via `charFun_convPow` for the `n`-fold row law). -/
theorem crr_log_return_tendsto_gaussian {r σ T : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < T)
    (hp : ∀ n, 0 ≤ crrProb r σ T n ∧ crrProb r σ T n ≤ 1) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => crrRowProbMeasure r σ T n (hp n).1 (hp n).2) atTop
      (𝓝 (bsLimitProbMeasure r σ T)) :=
  MathFin.crr_tendsto_gaussian_inDistribution hσ hT hp

metadata.reference: CRR to BS distributional convergence (Cox-Ross-Rubinstein 1979; Hull 21.1, Shreve I 3.2)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. The per-step CRR charFun is computed exactly from the two-point step law; its n-th power converges to the Gaussian charFun (crr_charFun_pow_tendsto_gaussian, via real cos/sin splitting of the complex exponential and second-order asymptotics of the CRR parameters); charFun_convPow identifies the n-step row law's charFun as that power; and Lévy's continuity theorem (ProbabilityMeasure.tendsto_of_tendsto_charFun) upgrades charFun convergence to weak convergence of the bundled ProbabilityMeasures. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/CRRCharFun.lean (crr_tendsto_gaussian_inDistribution). Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: CRR to Black-Scholes: Binomial Call Price Convergence (Closed Form)
theorems.description: The n-step Cox-Ross-Rubinstein binomial price of a European call converges, as n → ∞, to the Black-Scholes call price S₀Φ(d₁) − Ke^{−rT}Φ(d₂). The classical CRR→BS convergence theorem, completing the discrete-to-continuous pricing correspondence. No-arbitrage is hypothesised at every step with n ≥ 1; n = 0 is excluded because the step degenerates there (Δt = T/0 = 0 forces u = d = 1, where no-arbitrage is impossible), and MathFin.binomialNoArb_crr discharges the hypothesis whenever |r|·√T < σ, so it is satisfiable rather than vacuous.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.CRRClosedForm

open MathFin Filter
open scoped Topology

/-- **Cox–Ross–Rubinstein → Black–Scholes.** Under no-arbitrage at every step with
    `n ≥ 1`, the
    `n`-step CRR binomial price of a European call converges to the literal
    Black–Scholes call price `S₀·Φ(d₁) − K·e^{−rT}·Φ(d₂)`. Re-export of
    `MathFin.binomialPrice_call_tendsto_bs_closed`
    (`MathFin/Binomial/CRRClosedForm.lean`). The route needs no uniform-integrability
    machinery: the bounded *put* payoff passes to the limit under the distributional
    CLT (`binomialPrice_call_tendsto_bs`), binomial put-call parity lifts the limit
    to the unbounded call, and instantiating `bs_put_formula` on the limiting
    Gaussian lands the closed Φ-form. -/
theorem binomial_call_price_tendsto_black_scholes {r σ T S₀ K : ℝ}
    (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < T) (hS₀ : 0 < S₀) (hK : 0 < K)
    (hna : ∀ n, 0 < n → BinomialNoArb (crrUp σ T n) (crrDown σ T n) (crrPerStepRate r T n)) :
    Tendsto (fun n : ℕ => binomialPrice (crrUp σ T n) (crrDown σ T n)
        (crrPerStepRate r T n) (fun x => max (x - K) 0) n S₀) atTop
      (𝓝 (S₀ * Phi (bsd1 S₀ K r σ T)
          - K * Real.exp (-(r * T)) * Phi (bsd2 S₀ K r σ T))) :=
  MathFin.binomialPrice_call_tendsto_bs_closed hσ hT hS₀ hK hna

metadata.reference: CRR to BS call-price convergence (Cox-Ross-Rubinstein 1979; Hull 21.1, Shreve I 3.2)
metadata.formalization_scope:
Full formal proof of the headline CRR→BS convergence. Chain: binomialPrice_eq_integral_convPow identifies the binomial price with a discounted expectation against the n-fold convolution row law; the bounded put payoff passes to the limit under weak convergence (the distributional CLT of mf-crr-gaussian-limit); binomial put-call parity (binomialPrice_callPut_parity) lifts the limit to the unbounded call — no uniform-integrability/Vitali machinery needed; exp_neg_mul_integral_put_gaussian_eq instantiates bs_put_formula on the limiting Gaussian N((r−σ²/2)T, σ²T) through the standardisation Z = (· − (r−σ²/2)T)/(σ√T), and Phi_neg lands the literal closed form. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/CRRCharFun.lean + MathFin/Binomial/CRRClosedForm.lean. Axioms-clean. 

2026-08-20 correction: the hypothesis was previously `∀ n, BinomialNoArb …`, quantified over every n including n = 0. That is UNSATISFIABLE — at n = 0, crrStep T 0 = T/0 = 0, so u = d = 1 and BinomialNoArb 1 1 0 demands Real.exp 0 < 1 — which made the theorem vacuously true and its content empty, though the proof never exploited that. The hypothesis is now restricted to 0 < n, which is all the limit consumes (the proof already worked eventually-in-n; only the 0 ≤ p ≤ 1 bound needed n = 0, and that survives via crrProb_zero). MathFin.binomialNoArb_crr proves the restricted hypothesis holds whenever |r|·√T < σ.

theorems.name: American Option ≥ Intrinsic
theorems.description: Along every coin-flip path the discounted intrinsic payoff is dominated by the discounted American value: e^(−rk)·g(S_k(ω)) ≤ e^(−rk)·americanPrice(N−k, S_k(ω)) — the dominance clause of the Snell-envelope characterization at path level, routed through the identification theorem rather than the scalar Bellman max.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.SnellEnvelope

open MathFin

theorem discounted_intrinsic_le_americanPrice_thm
    (u d r : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (S₀ : ℝ) (N k : ℕ) (ω : ℕ → Bool) :
    Real.exp (-r * k) * g (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d k ω)
      ≤ Real.exp (-r * k) * MathFin.americanPrice u d r g (N - k)
          (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d k ω) :=
  MathFin.discounted_intrinsic_le_americanPrice u d r g S₀ N k ω

metadata.reference: American option intrinsic bound (Shreve I 4.4)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full derivation (upgraded-properly 2026-06-04): the dominance clause of the Snell characterization at path level — the discounted intrinsic payoff e^{-rk}*g(S_k(omega)) is dominated by the discounted American value along every path, proved through the identification theorem snellAux_eq_discounted_americanPrice (an induction over the tree, Binomial/SnellEnvelope.lean), not by le_max on the Bellman definition. Honest scope: this clause is the elementary corner of the characterization; the depth lives in the sibling clauses (supermartingale property, adaptedness, minimality over arbitrary path-processes) proved in the same module — see mf-american-supermartingale. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: American Value Process is a Supermartingale (Snell Envelope)
theorems.description: The discounted American value process X_k(ω) = e^(−rk)·americanPrice(N−k, S_k(ω)) on coin-flip paths is a supermartingale under the risk-neutral node average: q·X_{k+1}(up) + (1−q)·X_{k+1}(down) ≤ X_k — the conditional-expectation form E[X_{k+1}|ℱ_k] ≤ X_k on the finite tree, via the identification snellAux = e^(−rk)·americanPrice: the discounted American value is the Snell envelope of the discounted payoff.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.SnellEnvelope

open MathFin

theorem discounted_americanPrice_supermartingale_thm
    (u d r : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (S₀ : ℝ) {N k : ℕ} (hk : k < N) (ω : ℕ → Bool) :
    MathFin.crrUpProb u d r * (Real.exp (-r * (k + 1 : ℕ)) *
        MathFin.americanPrice u d r g (N - (k + 1))
          (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d (k + 1) (Function.update ω k true)))
      + (1 - MathFin.crrUpProb u d r) * (Real.exp (-r * (k + 1 : ℕ)) *
        MathFin.americanPrice u d r g (N - (k + 1))
          (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d (k + 1) (Function.update ω k false)))
      ≤ Real.exp (-r * k) * MathFin.americanPrice u d r g (N - k)
          (MathFin.spotPath S₀ u d k ω) :=
  MathFin.discounted_americanPrice_supermartingale u d r g S₀ hk ω

metadata.reference: American supermartingale property (Shreve I 4.4, Hull 21.5)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full derivation (upgraded-properly 2026-06-04): the genuine path-process supermartingale property of the discounted American value X_k(omega) = e^{-rk}*americanPrice(N-k, S_k(omega)) on coin-flip paths — q*X_{k+1}(up) + (1-q)*X_{k+1}(down) <= X_k, the explicit node-average form of E[X_{k+1}|F_k] (which on a finite tree IS the conditional expectation; same pathwise idiom as Binomial/MartingaleRepresentation.lean). Proved via the identification theorem snellAux_eq_discounted_americanPrice (the scalar Bellman recursion is the Markov instance of the path-space Snell envelope) in Binomial/SnellEnvelope.lean, where the FULL Snell characterization lives: payoff dominance, supermartingale, adaptedness (pathAdaptedAt clauses), and minimality over arbitrary path-processes (americanPrice_snell_minimal). Replaces the former le_max-on-the-Bellman-def shadow. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: American ≥ European
theorems.description: binomialPrice ≤ americanPrice for the same intrinsic g. The American option dominates the European with the same payoff — the early-exercise feature can only add value.

theorem american_ge_european_thm {u d r : ℝ} (h : MathFin.BinomialNoArb u d r)

theorems.name: CRR Drift Quotient Limit
theorems.description: For σ ≠ 0, (2 e^{rh²} − e^{σh} − e^{−σh}) / (h · (e^{σh} − e^{−σh})) → (r − σ²/2)/σ as h → 0 (h ≠ 0). Substantive analytic content of the CRR-to-BS drift correspondence: it is the step behind the textbook drift limit n · (2 p_n − 1) · σ√(T/n) → (r − σ²/2)T (substitute h_n = √(T/n) and scale by σT), which is not itself stated in this entry.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.DriftLimit

open MathFin Filter
open scoped Topology

theorem crr_drift_quotient_thm {σ : ℝ} (hσ : σ ≠ 0) (r : ℝ) :
    Tendsto (fun h : ℝ =>
        (2 * Real.exp (r * h^2) - Real.exp (σ * h) - Real.exp (-(σ * h)))
          / (h * (Real.exp (σ * h) - Real.exp (-(σ * h)))))
      (𝓝[≠] 0) (𝓝 ((r - σ^2 / 2) / σ)) :=
  MathFin.crr_drift_limit_h hσ r

metadata.reference: CRR drift convergence (Hull 21.1, Shreve I 3.2)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof of the h-form drift quotient limit. Building blocks: tendsto_exp_sym_sub_two_div_sq (via the algebraic identity e^{σh} + e^{-σh} - 2 = e^{-σh}(e^{σh} - 1)², reducing to existing tendsto_exp_sub_one_div); tendsto_crr_numerator_div_sq (combines with the existing tendsto_exp_sq_sub_one_div_sq); tendsto_sinh_div for the denominator. The n → ∞ form n · (2 p_n − 1) · σ√(T/n) → (r − σ²/2)T is the obvious substitution h = √(T/n) scaled by σT, deferred as routine algebra (the Lean expression for the substitution is intricate, the analytic content is identical to the h-form proven here). Lives in MathFin/Binomial/DriftLimit.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: CRR Drift Limit (textbook n-form)
theorems.description: CRR drift limit (n-form): n · (2 p_n − 1) · σ · √(T/n) → (r − σ²/2) · T as n → ∞. Closes the analytic content of CRR-to-BS drift correspondence; the h-form was shipped in mf-crr-drift-quotient.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.DriftLimit

open MathFin

theorem crr_drift_limit_thm {σ T r : ℝ} (hσ : 0 < σ) (hT : 0 < T) :
    Filter.Tendsto (fun n : ℕ =>
        (n : ℝ) * (2 * MathFin.crrProb r σ T n - 1) * σ * Real.sqrt (T / n))
      Filter.atTop (nhds ((r - σ^2 / 2) * T)) :=
  MathFin.crr_drift_limit_n hσ hT

metadata.reference: CRR drift correspondence to BS (Cox-Ross-Rubinstein 1979; Hull 13.4)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. Substitutes h_n = √(T/n) into the h-form crr_drift_limit_h, scales by σT, and closes the algebraic residual via linear_combination over the identity n · (√(T/n))² = T. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/DriftLimit.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Binomial Martingale Representation (Completeness)
theorems.description: On the binomial tree, every martingale is the discrete stochastic integral of a predictable hedge against the discounted asset -- market completeness, the second pillar of the FTAP.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.MartingaleRepresentation

open MathFin

theorem binomial_martingale_representation_thm {q : ℝ} {M S : ℕ → (ℕ → Bool) → ℝ}
    (hM_adapt : ∀ n, MathFin.PathAdaptedAt n (M n)) (hS_adapt : ∀ n, MathFin.PathAdaptedAt n (S n))
    (hM_mart : ∀ n ω, q * M (n + 1) (Function.update ω n true) + (1 - q) * M (n + 1) (Function.update ω n false) = M n ω)
    (hS_mart : ∀ n ω, q * S (n + 1) (Function.update ω n true) + (1 - q) * S (n + 1) (Function.update ω n false) = S n ω)
    (hS_nondeg : ∀ n ω, S (n + 1) (Function.update ω n true) ≠ S (n + 1) (Function.update ω n false)) :
    ∃ H : ℕ → (ℕ → Bool) → ℝ, (∀ n, MathFin.PathAdaptedAt n (H n)) ∧
      ∀ N ω, M N ω = M 0 ω + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N, H k ω * (S (k + 1) ω - S k ω) :=
  MathFin.binomial_martingale_representation hM_adapt hS_adapt hM_mart hS_mart hS_nondeg

metadata.reference: Discrete martingale representation / market completeness (Harrison-Pliska 1981)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof: pathwise node-wise representation, hedge = (delta M)/(delta S), telescoped. Lives in MathFin/Binomial/MartingaleRepresentation.lean. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: The Binomial Price of a European Claim Is the Cost of Its Hedge
theorems.description: Under no-arbitrage (0 < d < e^r < u) and S0 != 0, for every payoff g and horizon N there is a predictable strategy H (H_k depends only on the first k flips) such that, along every coin-flip path, e^(-rN) g(S_N) = binomialPrice u d r g N S0 + sum_{k<N} H_k (S~_{k+1} - S~_k), where S~_k = e^(-rk) S_k is the discounted spot.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.EuropeanReplication

open MathFin

/-- The binomial price of a European claim is the initial capital of a hedge. -/
theorem binomialPrice_replication' {u d r : ℝ} (h : BinomialNoArb u d r) {S₀ : ℝ}
    (hS₀ : S₀ ≠ 0) (g : ℝ → ℝ) (N : ℕ) :
    ∃ H : ℕ → (ℕ → Bool) → ℝ, (∀ n, PathAdaptedAt n (H n)) ∧ ∀ ω,
      Real.exp (-(r * N)) * g (spotPath S₀ u d N ω) = binomialPrice u d r g N S₀
        + ∑ k ∈ Finset.range N,
          H k ω * (discountedSpot S₀ u d r (k + 1) ω - discountedSpot S₀ u d r k ω) :=
  binomialPrice_replication h hS₀ g N

metadata.reference: Cox, Ross and Rubinstein (1979); Shreve, Stochastic Calculus for Finance I, Theorem 1.2.2 (replication in the N-period binomial model)
metadata.formalization_scope: Full formal proof. binomialPrice_replication in MathFin/Binomial/EuropeanReplication.lean: binomial_martingale_representation applied to two one-step martingales under crrUpProb u d r, the discounted tree value stopped at N (discountedTreeValue_step, from binomialPrice_succ) and the discounted spot (discountedSpot_step, from crrUpProb_mul_up_add), with nondegeneracy from d < u and S0 != 0. The strategy is the representation's node-wise delta. European payoffs of the terminal spot only; the identity is pathwise, with no measure on paths. Axioms-clean.

theorems.name: Reflection Principle (Andre, counting form)
theorems.description: Andre's reflection principle for ±1 random-walk paths: the number of length-n paths that touch a barrier a > 0 and end at b ≤ a equals the number of all paths ending at the reflected endpoint 2a − b. The combinatorial backbone of barrier-option counting in the binomial tree; the hitting condition on the reflected side is discharged by a discrete intermediate-value theorem.

code.lean:
import MathFin.Binomial.PathReflection

/-- **Andre's reflection principle, counting form** (1887). For ±1 walks of
    length `n` (paths `Fin n → Bool`), a barrier `a > 0`, and an endpoint
    `b ≤ a`: the number of paths that touch the barrier and end at `b` equals
    the number of ALL paths ending at the reflected endpoint `2a − b` — the
    hitting condition on the reflected side is automatic by the discrete IVT,
    since `2a − b ≥ a`. This is the counting backbone of barrier-option
    pricing in the binomial tree. Re-exports
    `MathFin.reflectionPrincipleEquiv_below` through `Nat.card_congr`. -/
theorem reflection_principle_count {n : ℕ} (a b : ℤ) (ha : 0 < a) (hb : b ≤ a) :
    Nat.card {ω : Fin n → Bool // MathFin.HitsLevel a ω ∧ MathFin.walkPos ω n = b} =
    Nat.card {ω : Fin n → Bool // MathFin.walkPos ω n = 2 * a - b} :=
  Nat.card_congr (MathFin.reflectionPrincipleEquiv_below a b ha hb)

import MathFin.Binomial.BarrierReflection

open MathFin

/-- **Binomial maximal-distribution identity** (running-maximum law). For a barrier `0 < a`,
the number of `n`-step ±1 paths whose running maximum reaches `a` is
`2·#{end > a} + #{end = a}` — the discrete `P(max ≥ a) = 2·P(Sₙ > a) + P(Sₙ = a)`.
Re-exports `MathFin.binomial_maximal_distribution_card`. -/
theorem barrier_maximal_distribution (n : ℕ) (a : ℤ) (ha : 0 < a) :
    Nat.card {ω : Fin n → Bool // HitsLevel a ω}
      = 2 * Nat.card {ω : Fin n → Bool // a < walkPos ω n}
        + Nat.card {ω : Fin n → Bool // walkPos ω n = a} :=
  MathFin.binomial_maximal_distribution_card (n := n) a ha

theorems.name: Binomial Price as an Expectation over Coin-Flip Paths
theorems.description: If the CRR risk-neutral up-probability crrUpProb u d r equals q ∈ [0, 1], then for every payoff g, horizon N and spot S₀, the backward-induction price binomialPrice u d r g N S₀ equals e^{−rN} times the expectation of g(S₀·∏_{i<N}(u if ω_i else d)) under coinFlipMeasure q: the Ionescu–Tulcea Markov-chain law on ℕ → Bool with Bernoulli(q) initial and transition laws (i.i.d. flips). The cylinder probabilities q^{#up}(1 − q)^{#down} are derived from the construction, not assumed.

import MathFin.Binomial.PathMeasure

open MeasureTheory MathFin
open scoped NNReal

/-- The `N`-step CRR backward-induction price is the discounted expectation of the payoff of
the spot path under the Ionescu–Tulcea law of i.i.d. `Bernoulli(q)` coin flips,
`q = crrUpProb u d r`. Re-export of `MathFin.binomialPrice_eq_integral_coinFlipMeasure`. -/
theorem binomial_price_eq_path_expectation (u d r : ℝ) (g : ℝ → ℝ) {q : ℝ≥0} (hq : q ≤ 1)
    (hqcrr : crrUpProb u d r = q) (N : ℕ) (S₀ : ℝ) :
    binomialPrice u d r g N S₀
      = Real.exp (-(r * N)) * ∫ ω, g (spotPath S₀ u d N ω) ∂coinFlipMeasure q hq :=
  binomialPrice_eq_integral_coinFlipMeasure u d r g hq hqcrr N S₀

theorems.name: Law of One Price in the One-Period Binomial Model
theorems.description: In the one-period binomial model with S₀ > 0 and 0 < d < e^r < u, the portfolio replicating a claim (V_u, V_d) is unique, and every portfolio (Δ, B) paying V_u in the up state and V_d in the down state costs ΔS₀ + B = e^{−r}(qV_u + (1−q)V_d), q = (e^r − d)/(u − d). This price equals the two-state pricing-kernel value whose state prices e^{−r}·(−z_d, z_u)/(z_u − z_d) are the discounted backward-FTAP martingale weights of the excess returns z_u = u − e^r, z_d = d − e^r. One period, two states.

theorems.name: American Call Equals European Call in the Binomial Tree (No Dividends)
theorems.description: In the n-step binomial tree with 0 < d < e^r < u, a nonnegative per-step rate r ≥ 0 and strike K ≥ 0, the American call price on a non-dividend-paying stock (backward induction with the Bellman maximum of exercise value and continuation value) equals the European call price at every step n and spot S: early exercise never adds value. The one-period continuation dominates the intrinsic value by Jensen's inequality for (·)⁺, the martingale identity qu + (1−q)d = e^r and e^{−r}K ≤ K; induction on n lifts it.

theorems.name: Mean and Variance of the CRR Log-Return Law Converge to the Black–Scholes Values
theorems.description: Let ν_n be the Cox–Ross–Rubinstein one-step risk-neutral log-return law (mass p_n at σ√(T/n) and 1 − p_n at −σ√(T/n)) and ν_n^{*n} its n-fold convolution, the law of the n-step log-return. For σ, T > 0, as n → ∞ the mean of ν_n^{*n} converges to (r − σ²/2)T and its variance to σ²T, the mean and variance of the Black–Scholes limit law N((r − σ²/2)T, σ²T). This complements the weak convergence of the same laws (mf-crr-gaussian-limit), which does not by itself give convergence of moments. For a boundedly supported law the k-fold convolution has k times its mean and variance; the CRR drift and variance limits finish it.
